items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Willie Smith, Benny Carter, Johnny Hodges, who was he listening to?

ctx.x: Tell me about Benny Goodman. How did that come about?

Well Loren Schoenberg was working for Benny at that time. He was sort of like his secretary, and, you know, fielding phone calls, doing things, whatever. But Loren had had his own — pardon me — he had his own band, and when, from what I gather, when Benny was approached by PBS to do a PBS special, “Let’s Dance,” he just asked Loren to put the band together, to get a band together. And Loren always had an interest, I mean his primary interest, especially at that time, whenever he would get his band together, would…

Benny had heard that band and says, “Get that band together.” I was pretty new in town, Loren knew me though. And I gather for the first rehearsal Howard Alden did the first rehearsal, and he was playing in that band at that time, but he couldn’t make the next one. And so Loren called me and I did it, and I don’t know if — for whatever reason — either Benny said let him go or Loren said you know I want to use this guy, but who knows, but I ended up doing it. So there you go. Yeah Benny. I mean everybody hears…
